slab_paved_streets.observation: The main street is laid with fitted stone slabs, and the mud of the rains no longer swallows carts and sandals.

cyclopean_masonry.observation: Blocks too big for any crew of men to lift, people say, are levered into the citadel wall and wedged with small stones.
cyclopean_masonry.social_consequence: The citadel walls awe friend and enemy alike, and every season of hauling blocks is a season the villages owe the palace.

corbelled_domed_tombs.observation: A long passage leads into a beehive chamber whose stone rings step inward until a single capstone closes it.

masonry_arch_centering.observation: A timber frame holds the curve while the masons set the stones, and it is knocked out only when the last one locks.

relieving_triangles.observation: Above the great lintel the builders leave an open triangle, and the wall's weight passes round the doorway instead of onto it.

corbelled_culvert_bridges.observation: Stone slabs stepped inward from each bank close over the stream, and wagons cross where they once forded.

ashlar_retaining_terraces.observation: Dressed-stone retaining walls hold the hillside in level steps for houses and gardens.

spillway_reservoirs.observation: When the reservoir fills, the surplus runs out over a paved stone spill instead of tearing through the dam.

stepped_spring_tunnels.observation: A stair cut through the rock leads down inside the walls to the spring, so the town drinks even under siege.

plastered_rock_cisterns.observation: Bell-shaped cisterns cut into the rock and sealed with lime plaster hold a winter's rain through the dry months.

stone_quays.observation: Dressed-stone quays let ships tie up alongside and unload over a plank instead of into small boats.

rubble_breakwaters.observation: Ten thousand boatloads of rubble dumped in the sea make an arm of stone that the winter waves break against.

flanged_interlocking_tiles.observation: Flat tiles with raised edges are laid side by side and capped with rounded tiles, and the roof sheds the heaviest rain.

iron_tool_rock_cutting.observation: With iron picks a crew cuts a chamber into the cliff in a season where bronze once took years.

pillared_storehouses.observation: Long storehouses with rows of stone pillars keep the grain dry and let the carts drive right inside.

canal_sluice_gates.observation: A timber gate raised in its stone grooves lets water into the town canal or shuts out the flood.

groundwater_tunnels.observation: A line of shafts across the plain marks a tunnel sloping gently from the foothills' groundwater to the village fields.
groundwater_tunnels.ability_reason: A tunnel graded just steeper than level draws groundwater out of the hills with no lifting at all.
groundwater_tunnels.social_consequence: Villages on the tunnel line owe days every year to clear its shafts; a neglected tunnel silts up and the fields die with it.

drained_intertown_roads.observation: The road between the towns is raised, cambered and ditched on both sides, and carts use it even after rain.

rock_cut_water_tunnels.observation: A tunnel cut through the hill brings the spring's water inside the walls, hidden from any besieger.

stone_channel_aqueduct_bridges.observation: Where the conduit meets a valley, a stone bridge carries its channel across on a single row of piers.

gravity_conduit_grade_control.observation: Surveyors set the conduit's fall with leveling staffs, a finger's drop for every hundred paces, and the water never pools.

crushed_pottery_plaster.observation: Lime mixed with crushed pottery sets into a pink plaster that holds water in cisterns and baths.

two_ended_tunnels.observation: Two crews dig toward each other from opposite sides of the mountain and meet in the dark within an arm's length.
two_ended_tunnels.ability_reason: Survey carried over the ridge lets two crews dig at once, halving the years a long tunnel takes.

public_fountain_houses.observation: At the end of the pipe the water pours from bronze lion heads into a basin under a columned roof, and the women gather there.

lewis_block_lifting.observation: A dovetailed slot cut in the top of a block takes an iron lewis, and the crane lifts it with no ropes round its faces.

pontoon_bridges.observation: Boats anchored side by side and planked over carry a whole army across the strait in a day.

excavated_harbor_basins.observation: The harbor is dug out of the shore and lined with stone, and ships lie safe inside while the storms blow past.
excavated_harbor_basins.ability_reason: A dug and walled basin gives shelter where the coast offers none, and a fleet can winter at home.

leaded_iron_clamps.observation: Iron clamps set in slots between blocks are sealed with poured lead, and the wall stands as one piece when the ground shakes.

timber_pile_foundations.observation: Oak piles hammered into the marsh until they stop sinking carry the warehouse walls above the soft ground.

rubble_core_walling.observation: Two faces of dressed stone rise together, and the space between them is packed with rubble and mortar.

ship_sheds.observation: Warships are hauled up stone slipways into long roofed sheds, and their timbers dry out between campaigns.

standard_lot_grid_towns.observation: The new town is laid out in equal blocks, each split into equal house lots, and every street runs straight.

windlass_wells.observation: A crank-turned drum winds the rope, and a child can raise a full bucket from a well too deep for arms alone.

street_gutter_gratings.observation: Rain and waste run off the street through slotted stone gratings into the covered drain below.

curbed_paved_streets.observation: Raised curbs keep walkers dry, and stepping stones let them cross without wading through the gutter.

aggregate_road_foundations.observation: Big stones at the bottom, rubble and gravel above, and a paved or rammed top: the road carries loads through the wettest season.
aggregate_road_foundations.production_contract: Build a layered road bed of large stones, rubble, graded gravel and a paved or rammed surface, matched to the ground. Crews, stone and continuing repair are required; the discovery builds no road.
aggregate_road_foundations.ability_reason: A road built in layers spreads each load into the ground, so carts keep moving when a dirt track turns to mire.

voussoir_arch_assembly.observation: Wedge-shaped stones set over a timber frame press on one another so hard that the arch stands when the frame is struck.
voussoir_arch_assembly.ability_reason: A true arch turns weight into thrust along its curve, spanning gaps no lintel could.

water_lifting_wheels.observation: The river turns a great wheel hung with clay pots, and each pot empties into the channel at the top of its turn.

distance_milestones.observation: Every thousand paces a stone post gives the distance to the capital, and couriers reckon their days by them.

harbor_beacon_towers.observation: A fire kept burning all night on the harbor tower guides ships through the reefs to the entrance.

screw_water_lifts.observation: A wooden screw in a sealed tube, turned by a man treading its end, lifts water steadily up the bank.

piston_force_pumps.observation: Two bronze cylinders with pistons force water up a pipe in spurts, enough to throw it onto a burning roof.

stone_arch_bridges.observation: The river is crossed on stone arches, and floods that swept away three timber bridges pass beneath this one.
stone_arch_bridges.ability_reason: Stone arches outlast any timber bridge and carry the heaviest wagons across rivers year after year.

vaulted_masonry_roofs.observation: A continuous half-barrel of stone roofs the storehouse, and nothing up there can burn or rot.
vaulted_masonry_roofs.ability_reason: A barrel vault roofs a room in stone, safe from fire and rot where timber roofs fail.

trough_leveling_table.observation: A long table with a water-filled groove along its top shows true level where a plumb line alone is fooled by the wind.

timber_roof_trusses.observation: Rafters tied by a tie-beam and struts form a stiff triangle, and a roof spans a hall no single beam could cross.

inverted_pressure_siphons.observation: Lead pipes carry the water down one side of the valley and push it up the other, rising nearly to where it began.
inverted_pressure_siphons.ability_reason: Sealed pipes let water cross a valley too deep for any bridge, rising again on the far side under its own head.

heated_public_baths.observation: A furnace below the floors heats the water, and the whole town bathes, gossips and does its business in the warm rooms.
heated_public_baths.social_consequence: The baths become the town's meeting place; they also burn a forest of wood each year and pass sickness through the shared pools.

arcaded_aqueduct_bridges.observation: Three tiers of arches carry the channel across the gorge, higher than any tower in the city.
arcaded_aqueduct_bridges.ability_reason: Stacked arcades carry a conduit across valleys at full height, so a city can draw water from hills a long day's walk away.
arcaded_aqueduct_bridges.social_consequence: The city now depends on a single long channel; crews must walk it forever, and a break or a siege cuts the whole supply.

timber_cofferdams.observation: A double ring of piles packed with clay keeps the river out while the masons set the pier on the riverbed.

aqueduct_distribution_tanks.observation: At the conduit's end the water settles in a tank and is divided three ways: fountains first, then baths, then houses.

raised_floor_heating.observation: Hot air from the furnace flows under a floor raised on brick stacks and up through flues in the walls.

hydraulic_lime_binders.observation: Lime burned from a clayey limestone sets hard even in wet ground, where common lime stays soft.

pozzolanic_binder_blends.observation: Lime mixed with a certain volcanic sand sets like stone, even under the sea.
pozzolanic_binder_blends.ability_reason: A reactive earth mixed into lime makes a mortar that hardens by itself, wet or dry, and lasts for centuries.

masonry_moisture_management.observation: A course of slate below the wall and vents under the floor keep the damp from climbing into the plaster.

mass_rubble_concrete.observation: Rubble and mortar laid in layers between timber forms set into walls as solid as cut stone and far cheaper to raise.
mass_rubble_concrete.ability_reason: Unskilled crews can build in rubble and hydraulic mortar what once needed a master mason for every block.

flushed_public_latrines.observation: Overflow from the baths runs beneath a long stone bench of seats and carries the waste to the main drain.

underwater_concrete_moles.observation: Timber forms sunk offshore are filled with lime and volcanic ash, and a harbor wall rises where there was open sea.
underwater_concrete_moles.ability_reason: Mortar that sets under water lets a harbor be built on an open coast with no natural shelter at all.

tenement_blocks.observation: Apartment blocks five storeys high crowd the city, and the law now caps how tall a landlord may build.
tenement_blocks.social_consequence: The city houses far more people on the same ground; upper floors burn, collapse and breed fever, and the poor live highest.

stamped_lead_pipes.observation: Lead sheet rolled round a rod and seamed makes pipes of fixed bore, each stamped with its maker's name.

brick_faced_concrete.observation: Concrete cores are faced with triangular fired bricks, and a wall rises faster than any stone mason could raise it.

columned_underground_cisterns.observation: A forest of stone columns holds up the vaults of a cistern big enough to water the city through a siege.

cross_vaults.observation: Two barrel vaults crossing at right angles leave the walls free for windows, and the weight rests on four corner piers.

road_tunnels.observation: A tunnel cut through the ridge spares carts the long climb and brings the coast a day closer to the capital.

glazed_windows.observation: Small panes of greenish glass in bronze frames let light into the bath halls while keeping the heat in.

harbor_dredging.observation: Crews with buckets on a floating frame scoop out the silt each season, or the river would close the harbor mouth.

domed_masonry_roofs.observation: A single concrete dome, open to the sky at its crown, roofs a hall wider than any timber could span.
domed_masonry_roofs.ability_reason: A dome of hydraulic concrete carries its own weight round a ring, roofing halls that no beam or vault could cross.
domed_masonry_roofs.social_consequence: The great dome proclaims the city's power to every visitor, and years of levies and quarry work are the price.

graded_weight_aggregate.observation: Heavy stone goes into the base of the dome and light pumice near its crown, so it weighs least where it spans most.

coffered_vaults.observation: Sunken square panels in the vault cut its weight without weakening the ribs between them.

embedded_relieving_arches.observation: Brick arches buried in the concrete walls carry loads round weak points, so a settling wall cracks less.

long_span_timber_halls.observation: Great trussed roofs of fir span halls wide enough for a thousand people to stand in beneath a painted ceiling.

clerestory_halls.observation: A raised central roof pierced with windows floods the long hall with daylight above the side aisles.

aqueduct_mill_cascades.observation: The conduit falls down the hillside through sixteen mills in pairs, each wheel fed by the one above it.
aqueduct_mill_cascades.social_consequence: One hillside of mills grinds a city's bread; the water they take is water the fields and fountains below do not get.

buttressed_masonry_dams.observation: Stone buttresses on the downstream face brace the dam wall, and it holds back a lake for the city's summer.

vaulting_tubes.observation: Clay tubes, each fitted into the next, build a light vault that needs almost no timber frame to raise.

squinch_domes.observation: Small arches thrown across the corners of a square hall turn it into an octagon, and the dome rises on top.

tile_banded_walls.observation: Courses of flat red tile run through the city wall every few feet, binding the rubble core to its stone faces.

iron_tie_rods.observation: Iron rods anchored across the springing of each arch keep its feet from spreading while the mortar cures.
